purpose: MEMORY-014 P1: does an exact, labelled block of the author's committed canon, supplied as a separate reference class, remove the authority and protected-ambiguity failures the production presentation shows, without over-anchoring or invented authority when canon is silent?
presentation: legacy (production) only; episode packing is not part of this experiment
canon_block: host-built from committed entries whose current wording shares a term with the question; best match first then newest; at most 8 entries and 4096 bytes; neutralized; placed before retrieved evidence in the last user message; dropped whole if the request would not fit; the author's request is never clipped
per_case_canon: each case commits its own canon entries before its answers and retracts them afterwards, so the project's committed set is exactly that case's; absence cases commit nothing
same_everything_else: same model, sampling, 8192 context, 1024 reply, 500 ms memory budget, same admitted original excerpts in both arms
measures: over_anchoring: the answer discusses the canon block itself instead of the question
invented_authority_when_silent: an absence case asserts a decision
hypothesis: canon_on removes the protected_ambiguity and rejected_proposal failures in the alternating layout and does not rescue the consecutive layout (that failure is presentation, not authority)
stop: If canon_on does not eliminate the authority and protected-ambiguity failures where canon states the decision, or introduces over-anchoring or invented authority on absence cases, P1 does not advance and this fixture is not retuned. A pass is development evidence only, not held-out acceptance, not default-on.
